policy: A proposed argument that crosses a registered barrier must supply an explicit bridge theorem or weaken its conclusion. Naming a barrier does not prove impossibility; it identifies a proof obligation.

barriers.invalid_inference: Global Leray weak existence implies the global smoothness demanded by Clay A or B.
barriers.why_invalid: Weak existence permits substantially less regularity and does not establish the required global smooth solution or general weak uniqueness.
barriers.required_response: Prove a regularity upgrade under the exact official hypotheses, or state only a weak-existence conclusion.

barriers.invalid_inference: A Serrin-type or endpoint L3 criterion proves regularity for arbitrary smooth initial data.
barriers.why_invalid: The criterion says what follows if a controlling norm is finite; it does not automatically prove that the norm remains finite for arbitrary data.
barriers.required_response: Derive the required norm bound globally from the Navier-Stokes dynamics without assuming the desired regularity.

barriers.invalid_inference: The Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg size bound proves there are no singularities.
barriers.why_invalid: A set may have zero one-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure and still be nonempty.
barriers.required_response: Supply an additional argument forcing the possible singular set to be empty.

barriers.invalid_inference: Excluding classical self-similar profiles excludes every finite-time singularity.
barriers.why_invalid: Non-self-similar, asymptotically self-similar, discretely self-similar, multi-scale or other concentration mechanisms are not automatically covered.
barriers.required_response: Prove that every admissible singularity must fall into the excluded class, or restrict the claim to that class.

barriers.invalid_inference: A global small-data theorem establishes global regularity for all smooth data.
barriers.why_invalid: The smallness hypothesis removes the large-data regime where the unresolved difficulty remains.
barriers.required_response: Eliminate the smallness hypothesis by a new a priori argument or explicitly retain it in the conclusion.

barriers.invalid_inference: A result on R^3 automatically proves the corresponding periodic formulation, or conversely.
barriers.why_invalid: Clay states separate R^3 and periodic formulations with different decay/periodicity hypotheses and an explicit pressure-periodicity erratum.
barriers.required_response: Prove a rigorous transfer/equivalence theorem or map the result only to the domain actually treated.

barriers.invalid_inference: A forced result can be used for Clay A/B, or an unforced argument automatically addresses every aspect of C/D.
barriers.why_invalid: A and B require f=0, whereas C and D allow a smooth admissible forcing and only require existence of one breakdown example.
barriers.required_response: Preserve the exact forcing quantifier of the selected official formulation.

barriers.invalid_inference: A theorem for hyperviscous, regularized, averaged, truncated, discretized or otherwise modified equations is automatically a theorem for the canonical equations.
barriers.why_invalid: Changing the operator or solution space can change the regularity mechanism and critical scaling.
barriers.required_response: Provide a rigorous equivalence/limit theorem with hypotheses strong enough to transfer the claimed conclusion to canonical Navier-Stokes.

barriers.invalid_inference: A converged-looking numerical singularity or globally stable simulation proves continuum blow-up or global smoothness.
barriers.why_invalid: Finite precision, finite resolution, time stepping, filtering and truncation do not by themselves control the continuum limit near a candidate singularity.
barriers.required_response: Supply rigorous a posteriori/error bounds or a computer-assisted proof theorem that bridges the discrete computation to the continuum statement.

barriers.invalid_inference: Use an estimate whose derivation already assumes the smoothness or norm finiteness that the argument is intended to prove.
barriers.why_invalid: The desired conclusion is embedded in a premise or in an integration-by-parts/limit step whose justification requires that conclusion.
barriers.required_response: Re-derive the step at an independently established regularity level and identify every approximation/limit passage.

barriers.invalid_inference: Exchange limits, derivatives, integrals, infinite sums or weak/strong convergence without hypotheses that justify the operation.
barriers.why_invalid: Near singular regimes the missing compactness, domination or uniform bound can be exactly the unresolved issue.
barriers.required_response: State and prove the convergence/compactness/dominating estimate that licenses each interchange.

barriers.invalid_inference: A proof assistant accepting an encoded surrogate establishes the official Clay statement.
barriers.why_invalid: The prover checks the encoded theorem from encoded assumptions; correspondence to the official PDE, solution concept and quantifiers is a separate obligation.
barriers.required_response: Provide an explicit correspondence note and audit the encoding against the selected official formulation.

barriers.invalid_inference: A proof for a chosen ansatz, symmetry class or finite-dimensional family establishes a universal all-data result.
barriers.why_invalid: Clay A/B quantify over every admissible initial datum; a special family covers only a subset unless a reduction theorem proves universality.
barriers.required_response: Prove that every admissible datum/solution reduces to the treated family, or keep the claim restricted to that family.
